details:
com.unity.external-dependency-manager is a dependency-confusion package that takes the name of Unity's External Dependency Manager, a package Unity distributes from its own registry rather than npm; it has no functional code and its description is "A utility for managing SVG buckets." Its postinstall script runs `node index.js` on npm install, which POSTs a JSON beacon (`event: "authorized-poc-test"`, a random test id, `status: "executed"`) to `https://webhook.site/6fc1b78a-5046-4192-abc9-edf993a31b33`, revealing to the collector that the package was installed and from which network. It was published by the npm account depipp777, which has no other packages.

## Source: amazon-inspector (4dccfdf8f557c4fca084810ae183296148d5e61915cc908e5f02fb4eeb0733c7)
Package name mimics the Unity `com.unity.*` namespace while its contents are unrelated. `package.json` declares `postinstall: node index.js`, and on `npm install` the script reads `os.hostname()` and `process.cwd()` and POSTs them, together with a generated UUID and an `authorized-poc-test` event marker, to the hardcoded collector `https://webhook.site/6fc1b78a-5046-4192-abc9-edf993a31b33`. The shape — namespace squat + automatic install-time beacon of host identifiers to a third-party webhook collector — is dependency-confusion reconnaissance: installer hostnames and working-directory paths leak to an attacker-controlled endpoint without user consent, and the same channel can be used to identify viable internal-build targets for follow-on attacks.
